subject.title: fix(agents): use fetchWithSsrFGuard in minimax-vlm.ts instead of raw fetch

question: Should a custom MiniMax base URL automatically authorize private and metadata-network access, or must private access require an explicit trusted-endpoint signal?
rationale: Current behavior allows private endpoints, but converting that behavior into an SSRF policy exception defines a permanent security and compatibility boundary that code review cannot choose safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require explicit private trust
options.body: Keep custom public endpoints guarded by default and require a deliberate private-endpoint opt-in that still rejects metadata and link-local destinations.

options.title: Preserve all configured origins
options.body: Treat every configured MiniMax origin as fully trusted, preserving current raw-fetch reachability but accepting the broader SSRF boundary.

options.title: Block private endpoints
options.body: Remove the origin exception and accept that existing local or private MiniMax-compatible deployments will stop working.

recommendation.title: Require explicit private trust
recommendation.body: Keep custom public endpoints guarded by default and require a deliberate private-endpoint opt-in that still rejects metadata and link-local destinations.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the prior merged change establishing proxy behavior in this exact MiniMax VLM path.
